input.rationale: The restart receipt is correct about the load-time fields, but its storage omitted the promise ballot that the covering witness persists, so the rebuilt node started in Phase::None instead of Recover. SequencePaxos::with queues a PrepareReq to every peer whenever the loaded storage holds a promise, which means a faithful restart of the witness node would begin recovery immediately. This update records that construction-time behavior and attaches it to the restart question so the unreadable decided suffix is scoped as the pre-recovery state of a node that is about to ask its peers for a sync, not as a node that sits idle.

knowledge.assertion: Restarting over the witness's stored fields keeps decided 4, recomputes accepted 3, moves the marker back to index 2 and makes read_decided_suffix(0) return None with length 0.
The load-time arithmetic that explains it: accepted is rebuilt as stored log length plus the marker while decided comes back unchanged.

Boundary on the receipt: because the probe's storage held no promise the node started in Phase::None, whereas the witness node had persisted a promise and would have started in Recover with PrepareReq queued to every peer.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::with reads storage.get_promise() during construction. When it returns a ballot, the node starts in Role::Follower with Phase::Recover and queues one PrepareReq carrying that ballot to every configured peer; when it returns None, the node starts in Phase::None and queues nothing. A restart that loads a stored promise therefore begins failure recovery at construction time, before any caller message or tick, while a restart that loads no promise stays passive. The accepted and decided indices are loaded the same way in both cases, so this only decides whether recovery traffic is sent.
knowledge.conditions: OmniPaxosConfig::build over an existing storage backend; the backend persists the promise ballot (MemoryStorage does, through set_promise) or does not, with peers taken from the cluster configuration; no snapshot is involved.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.

history.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
history.hypothesis: It is stuck. resend_messages_leader resends the StopSign Decide once stopsign_is_decided and resends AcceptStopSign only while the StopSign is undecided. send_decide resends with the last used sequence number, and even an accepted Decide cannot advance a follower whose accepted index is below the decision: update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx clamps decided to the flushed accepted index, so the follower stays at its old decided value. AcceptSync, which would carry the missing StopSign and the leader's decided index, is sent only in response to a Promise, and a stable leader sends Prepare only to peers that are not promised. The follower therefore makes no progress until leadership changes or the user reconnects it.

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. When sync_idx already covers the StopSign (the follower's accepted prefix includes it), accepted_idx becomes one greater than the follower's last log position. Since nothing may be appended after an accepted StopSign, decided can reach at most that last position and stopsign_is_decided (decided == accepted) can never become true for that follower. When sync_idx precedes the StopSign, the same +1 is correct and the follower ends consistent.

knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::with reads storage.get_promise() during construction. When it returns a ballot, the node starts in Role::Follower with Phase::Recover and queues one PrepareReq carrying that ballot to every configured peer; when it returns None, the node starts in Phase::None and queues nothing. A restart that loads a stored promise therefore begins failure recovery at construction time, before any caller message or tick, while a restart that loads no promise stays passive. The accepted and decided indices are loaded the same way in both cases, so this only decides whether recovery traffic is sent.

materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.
